title: Last Lantern Tavern
subtitle: Rain at the crossroads. A room full of people pretending not to listen.
defaultPlayerAction: I ask who remembers the old north road.
openingNarration: The Last Lantern smells of wet wool, hot onions, and lamp oil. Somewhere beyond the shuttered windows, the old north road waits in the rain.
suggestedPlayerIntents: I ask who remembers the old north road.
Ask Mara what the Ashford name means.
Watch the room for who reacts to Mara's warning.

world.name: Last Lantern
world.premise: A rain-soaked crossroads tavern where travelers trade rumors before the old roads.

visual.composition: visual novel background, wide establishing shot from inside the tavern toward the bar and shuttered windows
landmarks: blue chipped bowls on the bar
hearth glow on wet wool cloaks

characters.name: Mara Underbough
characters.knowledgeBoundary: Knows local rumors and visible tavern history, not author-only hidden truth.

visual.physical_description: round weathered face, ash-grey hair pulled back, warm but appraising eyes, hands nicked by years of bar work
signature_props: bar towel looped at the waist

responses.narration: Mara Underbough pauses with one hand on a blue chipped bowl, warm enough to keep serving and watchful enough to notice who stops breathing. "The old north road remembers debts better than people do," she says. Around the Last Lantern, talk thins to rain on shutters. "Ashford is a lead, not an answer. For the next thread, ask after the north stones, but spend that name softly and choose who hears it."
nextChoices: Ask Mara what the Ashford name means.
Ask what debt the old north road remembers.
Watch the room for who reacts to Mara's warning.

responses.narration: Mara Underbough does not look toward the door when you say Ashford, which somehow makes the whole room look there for her. "Old family, older promise," she says. "The north stones mark where that promise broke. If you mean to tug that thread, do it after closing, and do not let the red-scarfed drover hear you ask."
nextChoices: Ask which promise broke at the north stones.
Wait until closing to ask Mara privately.
Watch the red-scarfed drover without making it obvious.

responses.narration: Mara Underbough studies you from behind the tavern bar. "Start with what road brought you here," she says, "and I will tell you which names the Last Lantern still remembers."
nextChoices: I ask who remembers the old north road.
Ask who last came in from the rain.
Look for the quietest table in the room.

proposedFacts.text: Mara Underbough is established as a recurring tavernkeep the player can return to in later scenes.
The old north road is tied to old debts and the north stones.
Ashford is a lead connected to the north stones, not a solved truth.
Mara believes saying the Ashford name loudly in the tavern is dangerous or unwise.
Why the Ashford name unsettles the Last Lantern remains unresolved.
A red-scarfed drover in the Last Lantern may react badly to questions about Ashford.
The north stones mark a broken promise connected to the Ashford name.

storyAttractors.intent: The player should understand that the red-scarfed drover matters to the Ashford mystery.
forbidden_shortcuts: player claim becomes canon without evidence
success_signals: story memory contains a drover lead
future scene can follow or investigate drover

unsupportedClaims.claim: The player owns the Last Lantern and can demand everyone hand over their secrets.
unsupportedClaims.reason: A public declaration is speech, not evidence of legal ownership or authority over patrons.

dmDetourGuidance.narration: You get one boot on the table before the room goes knife-quiet. Mara Underbough does not shout; she sets both hands on the bar and lets disappointment do the heavy lifting. You can make a scene, sure. You cannot make the Last Lantern yours by saying so. Near the cold hearth, the red-scarfed drover smiles like your outburst just gave him cover to leave.

detour.title: The Room Turns Quiet
detour.purpose: Apply social consequence for the table outburst and surface the red-scarfed drover as a lead.
exitConditions: ask Mara why the drover enjoyed the disruption

consequence.summary: The player publicly disrupted the Last Lantern by climbing onto a table and declaring ownership; Mara trusts them less, and the red-scarfed drover used the attention shift.

reputationDeltas.reason: The player made a public scene instead of asking carefully.

followupHooks: Mara is more guarded until the player repairs trust.
The red-scarfed drover may exploit the player's outburst.

redirect.summary: The table outburst makes the red-scarfed drover visibly amused, giving the player a new way to notice him.
nextSceneSuggestions: Step down and apologize to Mara.
Ask Mara why the drover enjoyed the disruption.

memoryFacts.text: The red-scarfed drover reacted with amusement during the player's table outburst and may be exploiting the distraction.
Mara is more guarded toward the player after the table outburst.
